concept.title: What a person must look at first
concept.shortdesc: The categories the draft flags for human review, and why.

conbody.p: The draft is a proposal. These categories need a person to decide: accept, rename, merge, split or drop. None of those decisions has been made.

ul.li: : Split into gardening, growing and garden visits versus outdoor adventure, riding and days-out activities.
: Split into running, jogging and walk-run events and groups, and other outdoor sports such as riding and triathlon.
: Split into cycling (rides, adapted cycling, bike maintenance) and other riding or transport-hobby activities such as horse riding, pony treks and model railways.
: Split into badminton/pickleball/table-tennis-style sessions and squash court use, with Astro Turf pitch hire belonging elsewhere.
: Split into sports and fitness coaching versus personal, career and money coaching.
: Split into buying goods from community, farm or museum shops and getting help with shopping tasks, with borrowing tools and equipment as a third part.
: Split into social lunch and dinner clubs and food clubs where members pick up a share of low-cost food.
: Split into support and information for unpaid carers, and information about independent advocacy and safeguards such as IMCA and Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards.
: Split into performing arts (drama, dance, musical theatre, rehearsals) and disco, DJ and party entertainment.
: Split into job-seeking support (CVs, interviews, job search) and organisational or policy work such as HR policies and policy consultation.
: Split into help managing and obtaining everyday medication and prescriptions versus programmes to reduce harm from prescription drugs and substitute prescribing.
: Split people giving time as volunteers from people receiving visits or help from volunteers.
: Split into drop-in support and advice sessions, and one-off Q&A or welcome events such as post-screening Q&As and volunteer or interview sessions.
: Split antenatal, breastfeeding and baby care education for parents from training courses for professionals and staff.
: Split into visits received at home (home help, personal assistant, nurse visits) and visiting people in hospitals and care homes.
: Split general emotional and practical support from urgent mental health crisis support.
: Split into general multi-issue welfare advice (benefits, housing, health) and asylum, immigration and migrant advice.
: Split into people with eating disorders or compulsive eating, and women wanting to get healthier (control eating, stop smoking).
: Split into people registered with a GP in a named area (eligibility by area) and patients of a particular service or hospice.
: Split into walking-group participants by fitness level and pace versus people who use walking aids or find walking difficult.
: Split into gardening, allotment and nature enthusiasts versus history, heritage and arts enthusiasts.
: Split into offenders, prisoners and people leaving prison (and their families) versus victims of crime.
: Split into individual volunteers and people wanting to help, versus charities, community groups and non-profit organisations.
: Split into people needing food (food bank users, emergency food, meal support) and people or families simply described as 'in need'.
: Split into couples and partners (relationships) versus friends who join in alongside the main participant.
: Split into GP registration in a given area, and NHS connection (NHS staff or hospital patients).
: Split into people who provide unpaid care to someone and people who receive paid or unpaid care.
: Split into being or registering as a carer, and a carer or parent having to accompany or stay with the attendee.
